summary: Google requires a Cloud project and OAuth consent screen configuration for all apps. Production apps must have a public home page, verified domains, and may require a security review if using sensitive scopes. Testing and production environments should be kept in separate projects.

reason.text: The steps to create a project and configure the OAuth consent screen in the Google API Console are clearly defined.
reason.label: inferred
reason.note: Model judgement from the verified claims in this guide; not tested.

reason.text: Publishing requires domain ownership verification, a public home page with specific policies, and potential security review for sensitive scopes.
reason.label: inferred

access_ladder.name: Internal Development
access_ladder.allows: The application is restricted to users within the developer's own organization.

claims.text: Internal apps are restricted to users within the organization.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: These applications are private and restricted to users within your own Google Workspace domain. They are not accessible to users outside your organization.

access_ladder.name: Verification Review
access_ladder.allows: The application undergoes automated branding checks and sensitive scope verification.

claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: The automated review usually completes in a few minutes.

claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: The sensitive scope verification process can take up to 10 days to complete.

claims.text: The manual review process for brand verification typically takes 2-3 business days.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: In some cases, where a result cannot be automatically determined, your app may undergo a manual review process that usually takes 2-3 business days.

claims.text: Brand verification typically takes 2-3 business days.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Note that all apps must complete the brand verification step first, which typically takes 2-3 business days, if branding information has changed since the last approved OAuth consent screen verification.

claims.text: Published verified apps can be accessed by any Google user.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Any Google user can access. Required for public apps that request sensitive and restricted scopes.

claim.text: All apps using OAuth 2.0 require a consent screen configuration.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: All apps using OAuth 2.0 require a consent screen configuration, but you only need to list scopes for apps used by people outside your Google Workspace organization.

claim.text: You must obtain OAuth 2.0 client credentials from the Google API Console.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: To begin, obtain OAuth 2.0 client credentials from the Google API Console.

claim.text: You must create a separate project for production apps.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Google's OAuth policies require separate projects for testing and production.

claim.text: You must verify your app's brand information before it displays to users.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: For production apps, brand information defined in your OAuth consent screen must be verified before it displays to users.

claim.text: You must submit your app for verification if it uses sensitive or restricted scopes.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: If your production app uses sensitive or restricted scopes, you must submit your use of those scopes for verification before you include the scopes in an authorization request.

claim.text: You must own all domains associated with your project.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Google's OAuth consent screen verification process requires verification of all domains associated with your project's home page, privacy policy, terms of service, authorized redirect URIs, or authorized JavaScript origins.

claim.text: Every production app must have a publicly accessible home page.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Every production app that uses OAuth 2.0 must have a publicly accessible home page.

go_public.item: The home page must include a description of the app's functionality, as well as links to…

claim.text: The home page must include a description of the app's functionality, as well as links to a privacy policy and optional terms of service.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Your application's home page must include a description of the app's functionality, as well as links to a privacy policy and optional terms of service.

claim.text: Apps require verification if they are configured for external users and display a logo or display name on the OAuth consent screen.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Your app requires verification if configured for external users and displays a logo or display name on the OAuth consent screen.

go_public.item: Apps accessing restricted data from or through a third-party server must undergo an…

claim.text: Apps accessing restricted data from or through a third-party server must undergo an annual security assessment.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Apps accessing restricted data from or through a third-party server must undergo an annual security assessment by a Google-approved third party.

go_public.item: All apps must complete brand verification before requesting data access verification.

claim.text: All apps must complete brand verification before requesting data access verification.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Note that all apps must complete the brand verification step first, which typically takes 2-3 business days, if branding information has changed since the last approved OAuth consent screen verification.

claim.text: Authorization codes are limited to 256 bytes.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote:
Authorization codes
256 bytes

claim.text: There is a limit of 100 refresh tokens per Google Account per OAuth 2.0 client ID.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: There is currently a limit of 100 refresh tokens per Google Account per OAuth 2.0 client ID.

claim.text: Access tokens are limited to 2048 bytes.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote:
Access tokens
2048 bytes

claim.text: Refresh tokens are limited to 512 bytes.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote:
Refresh tokens
512 bytes

claim.text: Apps in the Testing status have a 7-day refresh token expiration limit.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: This status overrides certain standard OAuth limitations for the organization's users, such as the 100-test-user cap and the 7-day refresh token expiration limit for apps in the Testing status.

claim.text: Apps in the Testing status are limited to a hard cap of 100 test users.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Only users explicitly added to the test user allowlist can access the app (limited to a hard cap of 100 test users).

claim.text: Published unverified apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes are limited to a hard cap of 100 total users.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Additionally, for apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes, unverified app warnings (Danger UI) will be displayed to users, and a hard cap of 100 total users applies.

claim.text: Security assessments must be renewed every 12 months.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: apps must be reverified for compliance and complete a security assessment at least every 12 months after your assessor's Letter of Assessment (LOA) approval date.

blockers.issue: You cannot remove the OAuth 2.0 consent screen once it is configured.
blockers.fix: Ensure you intend to keep the configuration before proceeding.

claim.text: You cannot remove the OAuth 2.0 consent screen once it is configured.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: For security reasons, you can't remove the OAuth 2.0 consent screen after you've configured it.

claim.text: Do not use the Web application type for native or mobile apps.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Don't use this application type for any other application, such as native or mobile apps.

blockers.issue: Use of user credentials for server-to-server

claim.text: Do not use user credentials for server-to-server deployment.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Equally, you must not use, or encourage the use of, user credentials for server-to-server deployment.

blockers.issue: The project ID cannot be changed after the project is created.
blockers.fix: Choose an ID that meets your needs for the lifetime of the project before creating it.

claim.text: The project ID cannot be changed after the project is created.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: The project ID can't be changed after the project is created, so choose an ID that meets your needs for the lifetime of the project.

blockers.issue: Production OAuth clients must not contain test environments or local redirect URIs.
blockers.fix: Remove test servers, test versions, or local redirect URIs from production clients.

claim.text: Production OAuth clients must not contain test environments or local redirect URIs.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Google OAuth clients used in production must not contain test environments, redirect URIs, or JavaScript origins available to only you or your development team.

blockers.fix: Use HTTPS for all redirect URIs and JavaScript origins.

claim.text: OAuth requests must use HTTPS.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: OAuth 2.0 clients for web apps must secure their data using HTTPS redirect URIs and JavaScript origins, not plain HTTP. Google can reject OAuth requests that don't originate from or resolve to a secure context.

blockers.issue: Google can reject OAuth requests that don't originate from or resolve to a secure context.
blockers.fix: Use HTTPS for all redirect URIs and JavaScript origins.

claim.text: Google can reject OAuth requests that don't originate from or resolve to a secure context.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Google can reject OAuth requests that don't originate from or resolve to a secure context.

claim.evidence_quote: Google can revoke or suspend access to Google API Services and other Google products and services for apps that misrepresent their identity or attempt to deceive users.

claim.text: Google OAuth clients used in production must not contain test environments, redirect URIs, or JavaScript origins available to only you or your development team.

claim.evidence_quote: Google OAuth clients used in production must not contain test environments, redirect URIs, or JavaScript origins available to only you or your development team.

blockers.issue: Unverified branding can lead to decreased user trust and more revocations.

claim.text: Unverified branding can lead to decreased user trust and more revocations.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: If your app's branding information remains unverified, it might result in decreased user trust of your request for their data, which can lead to fewer user authorizations and more revocations later.

blockers.issue: Links to Google Play Store or Facebook pages are not valid home pages.

claim.text: Links to Google Play Store or Facebook pages are not valid home pages.
claim.label: official_docs

blockers.issue: Privacy policy must be hosted on the same domain as the application home page.

claim.evidence_quote: The privacy policy must be visible to users, hosted within the same domain as your application's home page, and linked to on the OAuth consent screen of the Google API Console.
